doors.note: WordPress home page (Slider Revolution hero, "Toronto’s Biggest Bathhouse for Men") with one EventON 5.0.2 frame (<div id="evcal_calendar_379" class="ajde_evcal_calendar … ajax_loading_cal">, shortcode in data-sc: fixed_month 10 / fixed_year 2026, event_past_future all) and evo_general_params carrying the nonce (n) and evo_ajax_url "/?evo-ajax=%%endpoint%%". No event text in the HTML. Footer: "105 Carlton Toronto, ON M5B 1M1".

The plugin’s own eventon_init_load call, replayed as a form POST (nonce + cals[evcal_calendar_379][sc][…]) for the page’s month and then for each later month to the three-month horizon (fixed_month / fixed_year / focus range stepped). The answer holds the frame’s rendered cards; every card carries a schema.org Event block (@id event_<post>_<instance>, name, url with a /var/ri-N night suffix on repeat instances, image, HTML description, start/end printed as wall clock with a fixed "+0:00", location Place "Spa Excess" / "105 Carlton", organizer). The reader drops the printed offset and applies Toronto’s clock. The nonce lives about half a day: a stored page needs one fresh read first. October was replayed once during recon; November to January are the validation run’s own answers, read from the scratch page cache.

recon.notes: Recon 2026-10-18: robots, the home page and one October replay by hand; the validation run of the same day (run 20261018-111647 is the replay of its answers from the scratch page cache) read the page again and walked November, December and January (2026-10: 19 cards; 2026-11: 46 cards; 2026-12: 49 cards; 2027-01: 34 cards). 147 cards in all, every one a dated instance (the plugin pre-expands repeats; no card states a rule). Distinct titles: Happy Hour (24), College Night (15), Date Night (15), CLIMAX! Fridays (15), Naked Night (15), Playground (14), Ski-Mask & Shiesty Night (9), Bears in Excess (4), Latin Night (4), Ryan Russell’s Protégés (4), Slammin’ Sundays RETRO Parties (3), Boned Up (3), Rough House (3), TNE: Totally Naked Excess (3), CODE RED: FF Night (3), Fetish Night (3), Asian Night (3), Sexual Health Coordinator (3), Chubs at the Tubs (2), SOS: EXCESS Spanks! (1), New Year’s Eve 2026: Ball Drop! (1). The run also fetched three card pages (events/bears-in-excess, events/playground, events/happy-hour) and the WordPress REST copy of the home page before it was stopped for the request budget.

coverage.basis: Feed door: every card the calendar answers with for October 2026 through January 2027 (the scraper’s own horizon), 148 cards of which 1 is the same card answered by two months (New Year’s Eve 2026, @id event_145866_2, in both the December and the January answer) and counted once. Each card is its own dated single; weekly nights appear once per week. Cards whose month answer the run fetched after the window end (January 2027) are documented too — singles are never window-limited. No "CLOSED" day markers in these four months. Past cards: the October answer begins at the day of the request (fixed_day 18), so nothing before 2026-10-18 was returned.

traps.label: Card urls ending /var/ri-<n>.l-L1 (e.g. https://spaexcess.com/events/bears-in-excess/var/ri-5.l-L1)
traps.why: The suffix addresses one night inside the plugin’s page script and is a 404 asked for directly; every night of a repeat shares the event page. normalizeEventOnCalendarHtml strips it, so the card keeps https://spaexcess.com/events/bears-in-excess/ and the nights fold on title + date, not on the url.
traps.note: Extraction is correct — the card is a real night — the trap is reading the suffixed url as a page of its own.

traps.label: Times printed as "2026-10-18T13:00+0:00" on every card
traps.why: EventON prints the editor’s wall clock with the site’s configured UTC offset, here +0:00 for a Toronto venue (cal_def.cal_tz_offset -240 says otherwise). Read as an instant, 13:00+0:00 is 09:00 in Toronto; the wall clock is the statement and the reader drops the offset.
traps.note: Not an extra event — a time-reading trap on every real card.

traps.label: /wp-json/tribe/events/v1/events, /wp-json/wp/v2/events and /feed.json
traps.why: The crawler’s generic WordPress feed probes; this site answers 404 to all three (no Tribe calendar, no events post type exposed, no JSON feed). Three live requests per run that find nothing — the EventON frame is the only door.

openQuestions.q: Card descriptions state cadences in words ("Playground … Every Tuesday"), and the Bears in Excess card names its organizer bearsinexcess.com. If a series reader ever quotes EventON descriptions, these weekly nights could become series instead of one single per week.

At urlDiscoveryDepth 0 the run still fetched the cards’ own pages as listing enrichment (3 of about 12 distinct event pages before it was stopped) plus the WordPress REST copy of the home page and three feed probes: 13 live requests for one home page. On a bathhouse host that answers slowly this is the whole per-run budget of a quiet calendar; worth an owner look at whether enrichment should skip EventON cards that already carry page, image, times and copy.
